Traditional Roast Pig for Tiki Christmas

Served at: Tiki Christmas at Pearl Harbor

Serves 10-12Prep 20 minCook 4 hours

Roast pig is a centerpiece dish for Tiki Christmas celebrations at Pearl Harbor, symbolizing abundance and festivity in Hawaiian culture. This recipe captures the island spirit with a sweet and savory marinade, perfect for a communal holiday feast.

Ingredients

  • 1 whole pig, about 20-25 lbs (9-11 kg), cleaned and prepared for roasting
  • 1 cup soy sauce (240 ml)
  • 1/2 cup brown sugar (100 g)
  • 1/2 cup pineapple juice (120 ml)
  • 1/4 cup fresh ginger, grated (about 1 oz or 30 g)
  • 6 cloves garlic, minced
  • 2 tablespoons Hawaiian sea salt (or kosher salt)
  • 1 tablespoon black pepper
  • 2 tablespoons sesame oil
  • 4 green onions, chopped
  • 2 cups water (480 ml)

Method

  1. Preheat your oven or pit to 250°F (120°C) for slow roasting.
  2. In a large bowl, combine soy sauce, brown sugar, pineapple juice, grated ginger, minced garlic, salt, pepper, sesame oil, and green onions to make the marinade.
  3. Rub the marinade thoroughly all over the pig, inside and out, and let it marinate for at least 4 hours or overnight in the refrigerator.
  4. Place the pig on a large roasting rack in a roasting pan and pour 2 cups of water into the pan to keep the meat moist during cooking.
  5. Slow roast the pig in the oven or pit for about 4 hours, basting every hour with the pan juices and remaining marinade to keep the skin moist and flavorful.
  6. Increase the oven temperature to 375°F (190°C) during the last 30 minutes to crisp the skin to a golden brown.
  7. Remove the roast pig from the oven and let it rest for 20 minutes before carving.
  8. Carve the pig and serve with traditional Hawaiian sides such as poi, macaroni salad, and fresh pineapple slices.

Tips

  • For an authentic flavor, use a traditional imu (underground oven) if available for roasting the pig.
  • Baste frequently to ensure the skin stays moist and develops a beautiful glaze.
  • If a whole pig is not available, large pork shoulders or legs can be used with adjusted cooking times.
